question.problem: Which of the following describes the $c$-level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}},$ where $c>0?$
question.worked_solution:
The level surfaces of the function $f(x,y,z)$ are given by the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =c \\ \sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2}} & =c \\ {x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-{z}^{2} & ={c}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get a family of hyperboloids of one sheet:

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}-\frac{{z}^{2}}{{c}^{2}}=1,\,c\in (0,\infty ).
$$
